name: Powdered Azurite
summary: In Hillsbrad Foothills, workers grind blue stone from Azurelode Mine into Powdered Azurite. Thun'grim Firegaze needs it to forge brutal armor for rising Horde warriors.

sections.title: A Rare Mineral Compound
sections.body: Human workers dig blue stone from mineral veins beneath Hillsbrad Foothills. They grind and pack it for trade and metalworking. A skilled smith mixes the dust with dense metals, making armor more durable and resilient.

sections.title: Forging Brutal Armor
sections.body: Horde blacksmiths prize Powdered Azurite for its strength in metalworking, though the mineral comes from human-held tunnels across the Great Sea. Thun'grim Firegaze is an aging orc armorer in the Barrens. He asks for small amounts alongside refined iron and fiery reagents. Mixed into the smelt, the powder helps him hammer out the heavy plating of his Brutal Armor.

faq.q: What is Powdered Azurite used for?
faq.answer: Thun'grim Firegaze mixes Powdered Azurite with iron ingots and volatile reagents to forge pieces of Brutal Armor for Horde champions.

faq.q: Where can Powdered Azurite be found?
faq.answer: Human miners gather Powdered Azurite in Azurelode Mine, along the southern coast of Hillsbrad Foothills in the Eastern Kingdoms.

faq.q: Why does an armorer in the Barrens require reagents from Hillsbrad?
faq.answer: Thun'grim Firegaze seeks fine materials for armor worthy of legendary warriors. Iron is easy to find, but Azurelode mineral tempers metal, so he sends his champions across the sea to obtain it.

angles.text: As a warrior, you test your endurance abroad while gathering Powdered Azurite for Thun'grim Firegaze. He needs the reagent to forge your armor of savage strength.
As a member of the Horde, you must strike deep into the Eastern Kingdoms and take refined dust from Alliance hands in Hillsbrad Foothills.
